reason: The section lists individual seasonal staff who should not be re-hired, and gives character assessments of two others covering attitude, self-interest and fitness to supervise. These were young people -- counsellors and programme staff, typically 18 to 22 -- judged by their supervisor in an internal document at the end of one summer. Publishing the assessments under their names in an indexed wiki would attach a fifty-year-old workplace judgement to them permanently and findably, for no historical gain: the argument the report makes about staffing does not depend on who it names.
embargo_basis: later of record date + 75 (1973 + 75 = 2048) and estimated birth + 100 (staff aged ~18-22 in 1973, so born ~1951-1955; +100 = 2051-2055)
release_conditions: the individual has become a public figure in a way that makes the assessment materially relevant
what_was_published_instead: The institutional facts were kept: that the 1973 report ends with staff recommendations, that most staff were recommended for unconditional re-hire, and separately (from the 1975 report) that a departmental director was asked to leave mid-season -- recorded without the name. See the ledger note on the 1973 document in kb/reread/ledger.jsonl.
note: NOTE ON THE SOURCE: the cached OCR of this report is itself committed to this PUBLIC repository, and has been since the corpus was added in an earlier session. This register does not change that and cannot. What it does is keep the material out of the indexed layer -- kb/facts.json and wiki/ -- which is where the practical harm would be. See kb/restricted/README.md.
